geometric_decade_spectrum.note: decade-spaced eigenvalues -> 1 stiff / ~2 at 99%, like real sloppy systems

verdict: Formula calibration: prescribed spectra with k flat-equal stiff directions return eff-dim(99%)=k, a uniform full-rank spectrum returns d, and a decade-spaced (sloppy) spectrum returns ~2. End-to-end: the finite-difference GN-Hessian returns low eff-dim with a many-order spectrum for the canonical sloppy sum-of-exponentials and eff-dim=d for a stiff full-rank forward model. The ruler reports low when the system is low-dimensional and high when it is high-dimensional -> the low eff-dim measured on the simulators is a property of the systems, not a methodological artifact.
